messages:
Maria: Quick heads-up — after landing the kernel-selection matrix change yesterday, we’re seeing a regression on mixtral-8x8 workloads with long contexts. Throughput down ~12% on our standard qps test, p50 roughly same, p99 up.
Jon: Can you paste the bench command and profiler output? I want to see whether it's attention kernel or KV path.
Maria: Ran the standard bench: 
```
./bench_runner --model mixtral-8x8 --kv-dim 128 --num-kv-heads 8 --kernel auto_select --batch 8 --seq 2048 --warmup 200 --iters 200
```
Profiler snapshot (summary):
```
throughput_tokens/s: 24000 -> 21050
p50_latency_ms: 26 -> 28
p99_latency_ms: 142 -> 198
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.78 -> 0.74
paged_fragments: 13 -> 49
attention_kernel: fused_attn_v2 chosen on 80% of layers
```
Jon: paged_fragments jumping that much smells like fragmentation in the paged KV allocator after the kernel switch. If fused_attn_v2 changed KV slot usage pattern we could be creating small free ranges.
Li: Also double-check RoPE scaling. We recently applied a RoPE scale tweak for long seqs (scale=1.06) which can shift perf profiles because some kernels expect exact stride assumptions. Any mismatch can change head_dim tiling behavior.
Sam: I repro'd locally. Changing kernel back to fused_attn_v1 immediately brought throughput back: 
`--kernel fused_attn_v1` -> throughput_tokens/s ~23700, p99 ~150ms. So the new kernel is correlated.
Maria: perf-bot, can you annotate continuous traces for the run with auto_select vs forced v1?
perf-bot: Annotated traces: linked in thread (perf-trace://1900123456/annot). Key observations: increased memcpy counts during KV fetch, more small allocations, and two kernels falling back to a generic attention path on certain head counts.
Jon: We should test two hypothesis in parallel: (1) kernel implementation changed memory access pattern causing paged KV fragmentation; (2) kernel selection logic mis-routed certain head_dim combos to suboptimal generic kernels. Quick tests: force kernel v2 but set `num_key_value_heads=16` and `kv_dim=64` to see if head alignment avoids fallback.
Li: I ran a small matrix: (num_kv_heads, kv_dim) 
- (8,128): bad w/ v2
- (16,64): perf ~equal to v1 w/ v2
- (8,64): slight improvement but not stable
So it looks like head mapping + kv_dim alignment matters for v2.
Maria: That suggests the kernel chooses a tiled codepath only when head_dim % tile == 0. If v2 assumes a different tile and we’re off-by-factor after RoPE scaling adjustments, we hit the slow generic path.
Sam: Reproduced fragmentation growth with a micro: random-length context mixes cause freed pages to be small and numerous. Paged allocator currently uses first-fit which amplifies fragmentation under that allocation pattern. Patch idea: add compaction trigger when free fragments > threshold or when avg_free_size < 4 * slot_size.
Jon: Can we try two quick mitigations: (A) change kernel-selection heuristic to prefer v1 for kv_dim 128 & num_kv_heads 8 until v2 is fixed; (B) enable aggressive paged_kv_compaction with threshold=0.25 for the experiment cluster. Anyone wants to own A & B?
Maria: I can push A (kernel-selection ibench flag) and run CI. Sam can toggle compaction in staging.
Sam: On it. Also adding a short test that runs a mix of seq lengths 256/1024/2048 to stress allocator.
perf-bot: Running staged job with (A + B) now. ETA ~25m. Will post numeric diff when complete.
Li: Another thing — check head-snapping in the kernel. v2 picks kernels using head_dim and kv_dim table. If we add a small shim to round head_dim to nearest supported tile at selection-time (not runtime), we can avoid fallback and keep semantics intact.
Maria: Good call. Let's avoid changing model params in prod, prefer kernel-selection changes first.
Jon: Postmortem plan if rollout impacted customers: document the regression, note temporary rollback to v1 for affected model profiles, and outline root cause (kernel-v2 head tiling assumption + paged allocator frag). We should also add a regression test to ensure kernel-selection doesn't pick a path that triggers fragmentation.
Maria: Notes for the run results (from perf-bot): 
- auto_select -> -12% throughput, +40ms p99
- forced v1 -> baseline restored
- forced v2 + head_snap shim (local) -> within 2% of baseline
- compaction enabled -> reduced paged_fragments from ~49 -> ~16 and improved throughput by ~6%

Sam: Action items: 
- Maria: revert auto_select default for mixtral-8x8 until we have head_snap patch (PR: rwd/inference#4219)
- Sam: enable compaction in staging and run long soak (PR: rwd/inference#4220)
- Li: prototype head_snap in kernel selector (branch: li/head-snap)
- Jon: add regression test in perf CI that runs mixed seqs and asserts paged_fragments < 25
Maria: I'll also file an ops alert so we can rollback quickly if any Canary shows degradation. @Jon @Li please ping here when you have prototypes.
Jon: Will do. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Sam: thanks :slightly_smiling_face:
perf-bot: Staged job complete. Summary: compaction + kernel-selector fallback reduces regression to -2% and p99 within 10% of baseline. Full logs uploaded to perf-bucket/1900123456/
